answer: Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, capped per identity per epoch, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. By the marble of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. Each submission hangs on the quill of a task receipt, and the bridge is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter.
